answer:
Headline results of agent run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (stride 20):

- Records analysed: 759 (2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z; 3.314% of the time window)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above Mc)
- Pumping over 15.96 days: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED probabilities (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — this is the calibrated estimate):
- b = 1.0:  Sigma = -5.449, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198, P(Mw>=5.5) per observed volume = 5.236e-06, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.03719
- b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.319, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922, P(Mw>=5.5) per observed volume = 0.0002155, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.2809
- b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.281, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474, P(Mw>=5.5) per observed volume = 0.0006484, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.4653

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes; every DAS detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts — this is NOT calibrated):
- b = 0.9849: Sigma = -2.698, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated (LBNL catalogue) probabilities of a Pohang-like Mw >= 5.5 earthquake are very low — at most ~1.5e-2 per year even at b = 0.65, and ~1.2e-4 per year at b = 1.0. The DAS-based upper bound of 0.07842/yr is an over-counting bound built from uncalibrated DAS magnitudes, not a calibrated probability.
